Why Tides Turn

March 1, 2024 · 5 min read · Share

Tides are driven by the gravitational pull of the moon and, to a lesser degree, the sun, which together stretch the oceans into two bulges.

Spring and neap tides

When the sun and moon align, their pulls add up, and the result is a spring tide with the largest range of the month.

When they sit at right angles, the pulls partly cancel, so the range is smallest; these are neap tides, and they arrive about a week later.

range = high_water - low_water
